DURBAN XENOPHOBIC ATTACKS

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Durban under seige....

Further information:
Cape Town - It was not necessary to call in the army to assist authorities in dealing with xenophobic violence that has taken grip in parts of KwaZulu-Natal, Police Minister Nkosinathi Nhleko said on Tuesday.

"The situation... has not come to that point to necessitate the point of army deployment," he told reporters in Cape Town and Pretoria via video conference.

"Government agencies have handled that situation relatively quite well in a sense [of] the collaborative effort."

Complex matter

He said the current violence in KwaZulu-Natal was a complex matter.

"Firstly, some of us find it difficult to think that this is just xenophobic. I think it also represents a particular political problem. You don't see Australians being chased on the street, you don't see Britons being chased on the streets."

In a sense what was being witnessed in KwaZulu-Natal represented a form of African "self-hate" he said.

Zimbabweans, Congolese, Malawians, Mozambicans, Somalis and Ethiopians were among the most notable nationalities being targeted.

"You are essentially dealing with an ideological problem that has to be tackled on all sorts of fronts and in this case you require a collaborative effort right across our society to fight off these kind of attitudes, and from within our society," he said.

Criminal element

There were also other factors which needed to be considered, such as the criminal element, where criminals were using the cover of xenophobic attacks to raid shops and break the law.

"These particular activities need to stop and need to come to an end," he said.

"We also need to interact among ourselves as South Africans on how we educate ourselves on matters of this particular nature."

He said there was continuing analysis of what was happening, and this would be used to construct a fuller picture of how deep the problem of xenophobia and related factors were.

Facing the full might of the law

Earlier, Defence Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula said government would take action against all criminals.

"As South Africans we should refuse to be part of the attacks on innocents just because they are foreigners," she said.

"We are equally determined to take action against all foreign nationals who commit crimes in our country. Each and every person working and living in the country must obey the law of the country."

She said it was also wrong to argue that crime was mainly committed by non-South Africans.

"A criminal is a criminal irrespective of nationality and [they] should be made to face the full might of the law," she said.

Press Release:


Foreign Fear
This week on the streets of Durban’s CBD, police battled to control looters as they forced their way into foreign-owned shops before setting them ablaze. Five people lost their lives - among them a 14 year old boy – and thousands more were displaced to makeshift refugee camps. Carte Blanche investigates the deeper issues that underpin this recurring violence.


Script:


XENOPHOBIA ATTACKS FINAL SCRIPT

VO: Xenophobic attacks have flared up across the country with police on high alert in KZN and Gauteng.

The latest attacks are in Johannesburg following nearly three weeks of unrest in KZN. Shops looted, vehicles set ablaze and foreign nationals forced to flee their homes.

Things turned for the worse on Thursday with a short lived peace march in Durban. Thousands took to the streets against xenophobia.

LINK: Everything was completely peaceful until right now, 13.35, and this broke out ....

UPSOUND COP: throw, throw, throw...

VO: Armed officers on foot, motor cycles and in armoured vehicles moved up the street diespersing the crowd and clearing the city centre.

Zulu King Goodwill Zwelithini has been accused of sparking the xenophobic attacks.

This audio clip is from a gathering in northern KZN at the end of March.

UPSOUND KING GOODWILL ZWELITHINI: We ask that the Immigrants must pack their bags and go where they came from.

VO: King Zwelithini blamed the media for distoring his comments. But the situation is more complex than just that says political analyst Prince Mashele.

LINK: This is chatsworth camp – one of the largest – up to 2000 foreign national – from all over Southern Africa – mainly from Zimbabwe and Malawi.

PRINCE: There is a combination of the call he made and real socio-economic conditions – He is a very influencial figure his people see it as a call to respond to their leader.

VO: Incidents flared up sporadically in the north, the south and to the west of Durban. Leaving at least 6 people dead, many more injured and thousands of foreign nationals displaced.

Tafasdwa: They start chasing you, when they found you the house, they beat you they just leave you, when you go then they start taking your things.

VO: Zimbabwean Tafasdwa, says it’s criminality masked as xenophobia, others like James, also Zimbabwean, feel it’s pure hatred.

JAMES: // they hate foreigners, they don’t want foreigners. We are qualified, so how can they say we are taking their jobs, you are not qualified – how can you do my job. He is doesn’t know the job, I am qualified.

VO: Both men were living in Bottlebrush, an informal settlement in Chatsworth, south of Durban. They say as many as five hundred foreigners this area.

We went back with them to the homes they abandoned.

JAMES: The hit the burglar bar – they hit it and they come in side here, they chase me outside, I was with my two younger brother – they hit my brother on the head, they hit my younger brother.
DEREK: is this your room
JAMES: yes

VO: Everything except the beds and cupboard were taken – his TV, hifi and clothes were gone.

What makes it worse for James & Tafasdwa is that their attackers were their neighbours – they never thought they would harm them.

DEREK: What happens now, where do you go now?
JAMES: nowhere, because my very friend was the one attack me, injured me take my things, he stay there, how can we stay together? We can’t stay together.

VO: Tafasdwa was heartbroken when he got to his home. The owner already put a new tenant in his house.

TAfASDWA: nothing insde when she came.
DEREK: empty, how do you feel.
TAFASDWA: Yah.

VO: Only his satelite dish remained – he took it down and made his way back to the camp.

Lawyers for Human Rights attorney Nomagugu Ngubane works with foreign nationals, she believes the most vulnerable are being exploited.

NOMAGUGU: I call them thieves, they are criminals who are taking advantage of the situation – some people don’t know what the term xenophobia means.

VO: Many of the foreign nationals in the camps feel they would rather be repatriated to their home countries. But Nomagugu says, it’s not always a viable option for refugees and assylum seekers.

NOMAGUGU: they have left their own countries, not even left – they have fled their own courntries for fear of persecution. // now what happens when we have this floods xeno attackes, it resonates with what they experience.

VO: Earlier in the week – Mathma Ghandi Road in the Point area was completely blocked off when foreign nationals took up arms. Tyres were burned and police the challenged.

The situation was eventually contained. Shopkeepers desperate to avoid attacks and looting moved their stock out of the shops. A heavy police presence in and around Durban, ensured that the night was relatively uneventful.

LINK: You can feel the tension here on Mathma Ghandi, the shops are closed, the store keepers are waiting for another attack – they say that they are here to fight

CONGO MAN: If you want to fight we will fight – we know how to fight – we are no more going home

VO: Ready for the next attack, many foreigners have started carrying weapons.

DEREK: What else have you got there? Can you show us?
DEREK: This can do a bit of damage.

VO: The whole community is on edge. Most of the shops in the area were closed.

CONGO MAN: This shop is closed, at the end of month I have to pay for this fucking shop.
DEREK: When do you think you’ll open?
FOREIGNER: We don’t know, if we open they come and attack us and loot….

VO: And this fear is being fuelled by videos and social media.

UPSOUND MAN SHOWING VIDEO: in this country.

VO: But none of the videos shown to us were actually from attacks in Durban or even from this year.

Unsubstatiated threats of retaliation from groups like Nigeria’s Boko Haram, Somalia’s al-shabaab and Mozambique’s Renamo are also doing the rounds.

NOMAGUGU: Basically sending out threats, ultimatiums, and just infliciting more fear, it is not clear where these texts are emminating from.

VO: As the world watches, there have been calls to boycott South African products from various African countries.

These attacks are being described as Afrophobia – but it’s just a diversion says Prince Mashele – the attacks are based on foreign fear.

PRINCE: This concept of Afrophobia is a coinage of South African politicians because they are embarrassed with their african counterparts.

VO: Some Durban locals are not embarrassed, they openly resent foreigners.

LOCAL: Firstly they sell the drugs, every fucking drugs, especially in point. They take our job that’s the second point and they take the less money than us.
DEREK: So they are working for less.
LOCAL: Yah for less. And they use the girls with the sexy there.
DEREK: They are using your sister for prosititution
LOCAL 2: the government he cant tax him, because no passport, no payment – you cant tax him.

VO: President Zuma appealed for calm and an end to the violence in pariliament on Thursday.

UPSOUND ZUMA PARLIAMENT: No amount of anger and frustration can ever justify the attacks on foreign nationals and the looting of their shops. We condemn the violence in the strongest possible terms.

VO: But while the President was speaking out, the peace march back in Durban turned to chaos with foreigners and locals clashing.

UPSOUND FOREIGNER: Enough is enough!

LINK: What happened next is that the local assailants ran up West, known as Pixly Kaseme, turned and met the foreigners on the other side – who are all apparently armed and dangerous. It’s a complete stand off with the police standing by.

VO: The South African government has warned the wave of xenophobic attacks puts the country’s interests both on the continent and the rest of the world at risk.

With an already strecthed economy – the violence and lawlessness could be detrimental to the country says Economics Professor Dr. Harold Ngawala

DR.NGAWALA: With the xeno attacks – we cant bounce back.
DEREK Come at the wrong time
DR. NGAWALA: This is not a good time.

PRINCE: For as long as these conditions exist in society – we will continue to have these waves.

FOREIGNER: People are dying in South Africa each and every day and government isnt saying anything – we are tired of this nonsense – it is better to fight and die.


STUDIO OUTRO: UPDATE ON WHAT’s HAPPENING – MOZAMBICAN BORDER CLOSED ON FRIdAY – SASOL evacuating South Africans form Moz.

PROMO 1 – 15 seconds
VO: Foreigners are fighting back in KZN - taking up arms following a spate of xenophobic attacks.

CONGO MAN: We ready to fight – we stand to fight over, we no more scared, and we no more going home.

VO: We were on the ground.

PROMO 2 – 15 seconds
VO: Attacks on foreign nationals have spread from KZN to Gauteng – violence and lawlessness seemingly masked as xenophobia.

NOMAGUGU: They are criminals who are taking advantage of the situation – some people don’t know what the term xenophobia means.


PROMO 3 – 10 seconds
Tafasdwa: They chase you, when they found you the house, they beat you.

VO: Thousands of foreign nationals after locals went on violent spree – attacking and looting.
